examples.en: I singed my bangs while grilling meat.
I lightly toasted the seaweed over the fire and ate it.

examples.ko: 가스 불에 고추를 그슬어 껍질을 벗겼어요.
examples.en: I charred the pepper over the gas flame and peeled it.
My sleeve touched the candle and I ended up singeing it.

examples.ko: 토치로 겉면을 살짝 그슬면 더 맛있어요.
examples.en: It tastes better if you lightly sear the surface with a torch.

examples.ko: 고기 겉만 살짝 그슬어서 접시에 놓으세요.
examples.en: Lightly sear just the outside of the meat and put it on a plate.

explain: '태우다'와 달리 완전히 태우지 않고 겉만 살짝 타게 할 때 써요. 햇볕이나 연기에 검게 되는 것은 '그을리다'를 써요. 'ㄹ' 받침이라서 '그슨'처럼 ㄹ이 빠지는 활용에 주의하세요.
explain_en: Unlike '태우다' (to burn), it is for scorching only the surface lightly without burning it fully. For turning dark from sun or smoke, use '그을리다'. It has an ㄹ ending, so watch for ㄹ dropping in forms like '그슨'.

examples.en: Maybe he has no appetite, because he just picks at his rice.

examples.ko: 깨작거리지 말고 한 숟가락씩 크게 먹어요.
examples.en: Don't just pick at it; take a big spoonful each time.
I'm worried because my child only picks at the side dishes.

examples.ko: 점심을 깨작거린 탓에 오후에 배가 고파요.
examples.en: I only nibbled at lunch, so I'm hungry in the afternoon.
Why are you just picking at your food?

examples.ko: 깨작거리며 먹으니까 먹는 데 한 시간이 걸려요.
examples.en: Because you nibble so slowly, eating takes an hour.

explain: 음식을 먹는 둥 마는 둥 조금씩 집적거리듯 먹는 모습에 써요. 조금 못마땅한 말투예요. 맛있게 천천히 먹는 것과는 느낌이 달라요.
explain_en: It describes eating in a half-hearted way, poking at food and taking tiny bites. It carries a slightly disapproving tone. It feels different from eating slowly and enjoying the food.

examples.en: You can get starch from potatoes.
If you add starch to the sauce, it thickens.

examples.ko: 녹말은 쌀, 감자, 옥수수에 많이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: Starch is found in large amounts in rice, potatoes and corn.
I coat the meat with starch and fry it.

examples.ko: 밥을 오래 씹으면 녹말이 달콤한 맛으로 바뀌어요.
examples.en: If you chew rice for a long time, the starch turns sweet.

examples.ko: 이 당면은 고구마 녹말로 만든 거예요.
examples.en: These glass noodles are made from sweet potato starch.

explain: 과학 시간이나 교과서에서는 '녹말'을 쓰고, 요리할 때는 '전분'이라는 말도 많이 써요. 감자, 고구마, 옥수수 같은 재료 이름 뒤에 붙여 '감자 녹말'처럼 말해요. 발음이 [농말]이라는 점에 주의하세요.
explain_en: Science classes and textbooks use '녹말', while cooking often uses '전분' too. You attach it to ingredients, as in '감자 녹말' (potato starch). Note that it is pronounced [농말].

examples.en: I ate a hearty breakfast and went to school.
Grandmother packed me a hearty lunch box.
In winter, dress warmly before you go out.

examples.ko: 시험 전에 든든히 먹어 둬야 집중이 잘 돼요.
examples.en: You should eat a solid meal before the exam to concentrate well.

examples.ko: 이번 일은 우리가 든든히 준비한 만큼 잘될 거예요.
examples.en: Since we prepared thoroughly, this will go well.

examples.ko: 점심을 든든히 먹었더니 오후에도 힘이 나요.
examples.en: I had a solid lunch, so I still have energy in the afternoon.

explain: 형용사 '든든하다'에서 나온 부사예요. 음식은 '든든히 먹다'처럼 배부르고 힘이 나게, 옷은 '든든히 입다'처럼 따뜻하게 입는다는 뜻이에요. '마음이 든든해요'처럼 마음 상태는 형용사 '든든하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It is the adverb of the adjective '든든하다'. With food, '든든히 먹다' means eating a filling meal that gives energy, and with clothes, '든든히 입다' means dressing warmly. For a feeling of reassurance, use the adjective, as in '마음이 든든해요'.

examples.en: My mom made kalguksu with short-necked clams.

examples.ko: 모시조개는 요리하기 전에 해감을 충분히 해야 해요.
examples.en: You need to let the clams purge their sand thoroughly before cooking.
I bought a bag of clams at the market.
The clam broth is really refreshing and clean-tasting.

examples.ko: 모시조개가 입을 벌리면 불을 꺼 주세요.
examples.en: Turn off the heat when the clams open their shells.
I made pasta with clams for dinner.

explain: 조개는 요리하기 전에 소금물에 담가 모래를 빼는 '해감'을 해요. 국, 칼국수, 파스타처럼 국물이나 볶음 요리에 넣는 재료로 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Clams are soaked in salt water before cooking to remove sand, which is called '해감'. They often appear as an ingredient in soups, kalguksu and pasta.

examples.en: Kimchi ripens well in the refrigerator.

examples.ko: 된장이 충분히 숙성되려면 몇 달이 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes several months for soybean paste to mature enough.
The longer soy sauce is aged, the deeper its flavor gets.
The meat was aged just right and very tender.

examples.ko: 숙성된 치즈는 맛이 진하고 향이 강해요.
examples.en: Aged cheese has a rich taste and a strong aroma.

examples.ko: 아이디어가 숙성될 때까지 조금 기다려 볼게요.
examples.en: I'll wait a little until the idea matures.

explain: 음식이 시간이 지나면서 맛이 자리 잡을 때 써요. 일부러 그렇게 두는 것은 '숙성시키다'라고 하고, 김치는 일상에서 '익다'라고도 많이 말해요. 생각이나 계획이 무르익을 때도 비유로 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is used when food settles into its flavor as time passes. Doing it on purpose is '숙성시키다', and for kimchi people often say '익다' in daily talk. It can also be used figuratively for thoughts or plans ripening.

examples.en: The braised ribs cooked until they were soft and tender.

examples.ko: 아기 피부가 야들야들해서 자꾸 만지고 싶어요.
examples.en: The baby's skin is so soft and delicate that I keep wanting to touch it.
The boiled chicken is cooked nice and tender.
After simmering it for a long time, the meat became tender.

examples.ko: 이 집 수육은 야들야들한 게 정말 맛있어요.
examples.en: The boiled pork here is really tasty because it's so tender.

examples.ko: 고기가 야들야들하지 않고 질기면 맛이 없어요.
examples.en: If the meat isn't tender and is tough instead, it doesn't taste good.

explain: 고기, 아기 피부, 어린잎처럼 부드럽고 연한 것에 써요. 보통 '야들야들하다'로 많이 말하고, 반대 느낌은 '질기다'예요. 음식 이야기에서 칭찬하는 말로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It describes things that are soft and tender, such as meat, a baby's skin or young leaves. People usually say it as '야들야들하다', and the opposite feeling is '질기다' (tough). It often appears as praise when talking about food.

examples.ko: 오늘은 제가 살 테니 양껏 드세요.
examples.en: I'm paying today, so eat as much as you like.
I ate my fill at the buffet, so I'm full.
Take as much as you want, as long as you don't leave any.
There's plenty of meat, so grill as much as you want.

examples.ko: 떡볶이는 양껏 시켜도 돼요, 제가 낼게요.
examples.en: You can order as much tteokbokki as you want; I'll pay.
If you're hungry, get more and eat as much as you like.

explain: '마음껏', '실컷'과 비슷하지만 '양껏'은 먹을 수 있는 양만큼이라는 느낌이라 주로 음식에 써요. '양껏 드세요', '양껏 담다'처럼 권하거나 허락할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is similar to '마음껏' and '실컷', but '양껏' means 'as much as you can take', so it is mostly used with food. It fits phrases like '양껏 드세요' and '양껏 담다' when offering or allowing something.

en: pickled vegetables (preserved in soy sauce or paste)

examples.en: I ate pickled chili peppers as a side dish with rice.
Jangajji is salty, so it goes well with rice.
This restaurant's jangajji is really tasty.

examples.ko: 깻잎 장아찌 한 장이면 밥 한 그릇 뚝딱이에요.
examples.en: One pickled perilla leaf is enough to finish a bowl of rice.
I bought radishes to use for pickling.

examples.ko: 오래 두고 먹으려고 장아찌처럼 절여 두었어요.
examples.en: I pickled it like jangajji so I could keep it a long time.

explain: 무, 마늘, 깻잎, 고추 같은 채소를 간장이나 된장, 고추장에 절여 만든 반찬이에요. 김치와 달리 짭짤해서 조금씩 집어 먹는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is a side dish of vegetables like radish, garlic, perilla leaves or chili peppers preserved in soy sauce or fermented pastes. Unlike kimchi it is salty, so people usually eat just a little at a time.

examples.en: I scored the sausage and grilled it.

examples.ko: 생선에 칼집을 넣으면 양념이 잘 배요.
examples.en: If you score the fish, the seasoning soaks in well.
Squid with scored cuts curls up like a flower.

examples.ko: 칼집이 깊으면 고기가 부서질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the cuts are deep, the meat can fall apart.
The sauce seeps right into the cuts.

examples.ko: 감자 겉에 칼집을 몇 군데 넣었어요.
examples.en: I made a few cuts on the surface of the potato.

explain: 요리에서는 재료 겉에 얕게 낸 칼자국을 말해요. '칼집을 내다/넣다'라고 말해요. 같은 모양의 '칼집'은 칼을 꽂아 두는 물건이라는 뜻도 있어서 문장을 보고 구분해요.
explain_en: In cooking it means shallow cuts made on the surface of food, as in '칼집을 내다/넣다'. The same-looking word '칼집' also means a sheath for holding a knife, so tell them apart by context.

examples.en: Please mix the flour and milk well.

examples.ko: 페인트 두 가지를 혼합하면 새로운 색이 나와요.
examples.en: If you mix two paints, a new color appears.
It's a juice blended from several ingredients.
This music blends tradition and modernity.

examples.ko: 세제를 혼합해서 쓰면 위험할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Mixing cleaning products can be dangerous.
Mix the two doughs and wait 30 minutes.

explain: 요리책·설명서·과학 글에 자주 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '섞다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '밥에 나물을 섞어 먹어요'처럼요. '혼합물'(mixture), '혼합복식'(mixed doubles)처럼 합친 말로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It appears often in recipes, instructions and science writing, while in everyday talk 섞다 sounds much more natural, as in '밥에 나물을 섞어 먹어요'. It also shows up in compounds such as 혼합물 (a mixture) and 혼합복식 (mixed doubles).
